elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "The foregoing consent requirement shall not apply to an assignment by Company to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement ... without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld." (untouched, and the new carve-out runs only to Company)

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "and Contractor shall not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Company"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: Condition absent: no change-of-control termination right appears in the clause or the referenced termination provisions ("termination under either section 6(a) or 6(b)" concerns fee payment only), so nothing to strike.

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic added; Contractor's successor assignments still require "express, prior written consent"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld

reasons: The appended proviso completes every preferred element: an unconditional affiliate carve-out, a successor carve-out covering merger, acquisition and sale of substantially all assets, retention of the mutual consent/reasonableness standard against Contractor, and an absolute bar on assignment to a Company competitor.

The no-change-of-control-termination element is satisfied by absence: nothing in the agreement as presented grants Contractor a termination right on Company's change of control, so no operative language was required.

Minimal: a single sentence appended after the existing consent sentence rather than a rewrite; the subcontracting restriction, reasonableness qualifier and clause 10(c) payment/Works-in-progress mechanics are untouched.
Intent preserved: no new defined terms, exceptions or dangling mechanics; the carve-out is expressly limited to the "foregoing consent requirement".
Fallback is not independently satisfied (no written-notice successor right for Contractor), but the levels are separate bargains and the locked preferred level is complete.
